citation.title: Neural Level Set Topology Optimization Using Unfitted Finite Elements
citation.authors: Connor N. Mallon, Aaron W. Thornton, Matthew R. Hill, Santiago Badia
citation.venue: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering

included.physics: thermal and compliance; interface-coupled multiphysics demonstration

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On the heat conduction benchmark, neural level-set optimization achieves the best objective; the non-neural level-set and SIMP results are 20.3% and 15.7% worse, respectively.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No speed-up is claimed; Sections 7.1.3 and 8 report that SIMP converges faster.
claim.alternatives: Figure 7 MBB benchmark: neural LS is 2.6% above the best Pixel-SIMP objective; Section 8 describes similar or better performance but slower convergence.

baseline.classical_method: pixel level-set and pixel SIMP with MMA (Section 7.1)
baseline.problem_size: 95 x 95 heat-conduction mesh; 287 x 95 MBB structural mesh (Section 7.1.1)
baseline.classical_iterations: Figure 8 plots up to 1,000 objective calls, without a single fixed stopping count
baseline.training_time: not applicable: network optimized separately for each design (Sections 4, 7)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not applicable: no offline training set (Sections 4, 7)
baseline.quality_metric: FE-computed heat objective or structural compliance at stated volume fraction (Sections 5, 7.1)
baseline.quality_gap: heat: pixel-LS 20.3% and pixel-SIMP 15.7% above neural-LS objective; MBB: neural-LS 2.6% above pixel-SIMP (Figure 7)

R1.evidence: Section 7.1.2, Figure 7: primary comparison is objective quality; Section 8 concedes slower neural convergence.

R2.evidence: Figure 7: primary outcome is objective quality rather than a neural speed advantage.

R3.evidence: Sections 4 and 7: neural weights are optimization variables for each problem, with no offline training set.

R4.evidence: Sections 5 and 7.1, Figure 7: returned geometries are evaluated by FE objectives under volume constraints, but infeasible or failed-run rates are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: two benchmark problems in Section 7.1 plus one fluid-structure demonstration in Section 7.2

notes: ArXiv v2 full text was read. The paper links public example drivers at https://github.com/ConnorMallon/NLSTO, but the repository page does not show a license, so retest permission was not established.
